text:
maria: heads-up — after the control-plane upgrade in eu-west-1 the cluster-autoscaler didn't pick up nodes from the gpu-tenant provisioner. several jobs pending and cost alarm fired :warning:

alex: copy. can you paste the provisioner object and autoscaler logs?

maria: here's the provisioner metadata we saw:
```
$ kubectl -n kube-system get provisioner gpu-tenant -o yaml
metadata:
  name: gpu-tenant
  annotations:
    provisioner.redwood/tenant: gpu-team
    creationTimestamp: "2026-03-12T08:23:11Z"
spec: {}
```
Notice the annotation key is `provisioner.redwood/tenant` now (post-upgrade). autoscaler selector expects `node.k8s.aws/tenant`.

jordan: that explains it — autoscaler matches provisioner by annotation selector. did the upgrade change the provisioner controller or our annotation migration?

deploy-bot: Cluster control-plane upgrade to v1.28.2 completed for eu-west-1 at 2026-03-12T08:20:47Z :rocket:

lee: quick mitigation: we can patch the cluster-autoscaler to add a fallback selector that looks for the new key, or temporarily patch provisioner to include the old annotation as well. which is lower risk?

alex: fallback selector in autoscaler is safer short-term. example patch for the deployment config:
```sh
kubectl -n kube-system patch deploy cluster-autoscaler --type='json' -p='[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/env/-","value":{"name":"PROVISIONER_ANNOTATION_FALLBACK","value":"provisioner.redwood/tenant"}}]'
```
(we'll actually bake this into the CA config map, not env var — just showing intent)

sre-oncall: what's the risk of leaving provisioner annotated both ways? any downstream consumer that relies on the old key?

maria: low risk for now. but we should avoid manual dual-annotation long-term. root cause: in the provisioner controller refactor the annotation key was renamed for clearer ownership. autoscaler code was not updated to check the new annotation key — regression introduced by the 1.28 rollout.

jordan: PR opened to autoscaler repo to try both keys (old first, fallback to new). test added. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/cluster-autoscaler/pull/742 (internal) :eyes:

alex: hotfix workflow ready. image build: cluster-autoscaler:v1.2.1-hotfix-annot-fallback. plan to roll in canary to eu-west first. commands:
```sh
kubectl -n kube-system set image deploy/cluster-autoscaler cluster-autoscaler=ghcr.io/redwood/cluster-autoscaler:v1.2.1-hotfix-annot-fallback
```

infra-bot: canary rollout started for cluster-autoscaler:v1.2.1-hotfix-annot-fallback in eu-west-1 at 2026-03-12T09:02:13Z

maria: after canary the scale-up resumed for the gpu-node-groups. confirmation from k9s: new nodes joined and pending pods scheduled. monitoring shows pending queue drained in ~8m :thumbsup:

lee: will follow up with migration plan to standardize on `provisioner.redwood/tenant` across infra and update infra provisioning docs. also scheduling a post-upgrade test to catch annotation-key drift next time.

sre-oncall: leaving this open until we've rolled the fix to prod clusters and added the e2e. created incident card and slack alarm rule to trigger next time similar mismatch occurs.

maria: thanks all. saving logs and keeping the hotfix for 24h then promoting to stable if no regressions. filing postmortem notes and owners. :white_check_mark:
